Welcome to St. Helen’s College
Hillingdon’s leading co-educational independent prep school
St. Helen’s College is an outstanding independent prep school and nursery for boys and girls aged from 2-11 years of age, with excellent all-round pupil development and academic results.
Explore St. Helen's College
Our entry points
At St. Helen’s College we have a thriving Nursery which admits children from the age of 2+ into Ducklings and from 3+ into Cygnets. Entry into Reception is from the age of 4 and we encourage early registrations as we are a very popular school and demand is high.
Nursery
Pre-Prep
Prep
Inspiring Minds, Shaping Futures
Explore our approach to learning
Every lesson is designed to challenge, engage and inspire, with quality teaching at its core. Beyond acquiring knowledge, pupils develop the ability to learn effectively. They engage in self-reflection, identify their strengths, set meaningful goals, and gain a deep understanding of the learning process.
Explore our approach to learning
A warm welcome
A very warm welcome from our Head, Ms. Sophie Green
We believe that we have something unique and special to offer the children who attend our school.
For 100 years, St. Helen’s College has been renowned for its family atmosphere and its warm, welcoming environment. We pride ourselves on the exceptional care and attention we give to each individual pupil, encouraging them to be the best they can possibly be. Our pupils strive for and achieve excellence, not only academically but in their all-round endeavours too.
St. Helen’s College children are known locally for their courtesy and manners, their impeccable behaviour, and for their impressive achievements, not least in gaining places at top independent and grammar schools.
Get to know our school
What sets St. Helen’s College apart?

Ms. Sophie Green
Sophie began her Headship at Herries Preparatory School in Cookham Dean, a co-educational setting for pupils aged 3–11, before joining Godstowe, a leading Prep school for girls. During her tenure at Godstowe, she successfully guided pupils through the Buckinghamshire 11+ grammar school process and in recognition of her leadership, she was named Tatler magazine ‘Prep Head of the Year’ in her final year. After leaving Godstowe in 2022, Sophie joined St. Helen’s College as Head in 2025. She is a trained and experienced ISI Inspector. Beyond school life, Sophie enjoys reading detective novels, cooking, walking, going to the gym, visiting art galleries, and travelling.
Ms. Jo Matthews
A graduate in Psychology, Jo began her career as an Assistant Psychologist, supporting young children with a range of special educational needs. It was here that she discovered her passion for teaching in early years. After gaining her teaching degree, Jo went on to lead a team across several schools in Staffordshire, in a pilot Government initiative to bring improved reading and phonics provision into primary schools, before joining St. Helen’s College in 2005 as a Reception teacher. During her time at the school, she has taken the lead in computing, CPD and early years. In 2013, Jo gained Chartered Teacher Status with the Chartered College of Teaching and now supports them as a Research Champion. More recently, she undertook further studies, completing a master’s degree in early years education. Beyond school, Jo enjoys illustration, literature, attending the theatre, and spending time on family holidays with her partner and two teenage children.
Mr. Steve Roche
Deputy Head Academic
Steve has worked across a number of independent school settings, developing a deep passion for the sector and its holistic approach to education. He began his leadership journey as Head of English, before progressing to his current role, where he oversees curriculum innovation, teaching and learning strategies, and academic standards. A published children’s book author, Steve brings creativity and a love of literature into his work, inspiring pupils to think critically and imaginatively. He values the warm, nurturing atmosphere at St. Helen’s College and is committed to fostering pupil wellbeing, drawing on his interest in mindfulness and psychology to support both staff and students. Beyond school life, Steve enjoys hiking, reading, and exploring tea culture.
Mrs. Melanie Gilbert
Deputy Head Pastoral
Melanie began her career at St Hilda’s School in Bushey, an independent prep school for girls aged 3-11. During her time at the school, she held the roles of Head of House and Assessment Coordinator as a member of the Senior Leadership Team, which provided her with a strong foundation in pastoral care and teaching and learning. Melanie also led the school in becoming one of the pioneer schools for Empathy Lab, an organisation that uses literature to build children’s empathy, helping them to understand others and contribute to a kinder society. She was appointed as Deputy Head of St Hilda’s School in September 2022 and joined St. Helen’s College in 2025. Melanie is passionate about creating opportunities for every child to flourish, placing their wellbeing and pastoral care at the heart of everything she does. Outside of work, she enjoys running, going to the theatre, dog walking, reading and travelling.
Mrs. Elaine Coyle
Elaine began her career in childcare 23 years ago and has been working at St. Helen’s College for 14 years. She has worked across the Lower School including the 2+ and 3+ Nursery settings, as well as in Reception, and managed the school Holiday Club for three years. Elaine is passionate about working with young children to provide a high-quality Early Years education and positive start to their school life. Elaine was appointed Nursery Manager at the new year-round St. Helen’s College provision in 2025. She is a trained Mini Me Yoga practitioner and outside of school she enjoys looking after her horses, dogs and chickens, meeting up with friends and reading.

Nursery
Welcome to Nursery
Where curiosity begins and confidence grows.
Selecting the right Nursery for your child is one of the most important decisions you will make. At St. Helen’s College Nursery, we are dedicated to providing the highest standard of care in our warm, stimulating and nurturing setting where every child can grow, learn, and thrive.
Our Nursery is more than just a place to play – it is where the foundations for lifelong learning are built. Through a blend of structured activities and free exploration, we inspire curiosity, creativity, and confidence in every child. Our passionate and experienced practitioners work in partnership with each family, ensuring that every child receives personal attention, helping them develop key skills in language, social interaction, and independence.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Pre-Prep - St. Helen's College
pageCache.text:
Pre-Prep
Welcome to Pre-Prep
Learning never stands still at St. Helen’s College Pre-Prep
Our Nursery, Reception and Year 1 children build strong foundations for lifelong learning in reading, writing, mathematics and science – providing the essential tools that enable them to understand the world, think critically, and communicate effectively. While a focus on academic achievement is key to success, we believe that opportunities beyond the curriculum are just as important for every child’s happiness and development.
Character education is sensitively woven throughout the curriculum, shaping teaching and learning. This approach helps our children develop not only intellectual skills but also a deeper understanding of wider values, such as kindness and empathy, and fosters a sense of responsibility toward themselves, others, and the world.
Together, these core areas establish the intellectual and cognitive foundations upon which all other learning can grow. Our children gain confidence and competence in these fundamental subjects and stand better prepared to explore broader disciplines, engage with complex ideas, and contribute meaningfully to their communities.
From thoughtful interactions during circle time to reflections in mindfulness or discussing ‘big’ philosophical ideas, our children grow into active learners who approach the world with wonder and curiosity. Every learning opportunity is carefully planned to allow our children to question, debate, collaborate and problem-solve from a very young age.
We believe in making learning active so that every child wants to learn more, and opportunities are built into the curriculum to give our children the confidence and motivation to embrace the next steps in their educational journey.
At St. Helen’s College Pre-Prep, our core values are lived every day: excellence, harmony, spirituality and growth. Together, we create a warm and welcoming environment where a love of learning and a strong sense of self is nurtured, and where every child feels safe, secure, and valued.
I look forward to welcoming you to our calm and purposeful Pre-Prep surroundings and to sharing in a vibrant start to your child’s education journey.
Ms. Jo Matthews

pageCache.pageTitle: Aims, Ethos & Values - St. Helen's College
pageCache.text:
About Us
Aims, Ethos & Values
School Aims and Ethos
At St. Helen’s College, we inspire a lifelong love of learning, fully nurturing each child’s academic potential, creativity and self-awareness. Rooted in our core values of excellence, harmony, spirituality and growth, we foster virtue, resilience, independence and compassion. Together, we cultivate confident, responsible and caring individuals ready to lead and contribute meaningfully to society.
Excellence
At St. Helen’s College excellence is at the heart of everything we do. We are committed to delivering an outstanding all round education and have an enviable track record of inspiring achievement and excellence in all of our pupils.
Harmony
Pupils’ wellbeing is of paramount importance to us all. Children learn best when they feel safe, secure and nurtured. A strong sense of harmony at St. Helen’s College embraces children, staff and parents. Our family ethos is nurtured by a culture in which staff and pupils enjoy friendly but respectful relationships.
Spirituality
At St. Helen’s College, children are encouraged to look beyond themselves, appreciate others and the world around them, and develop gratitude and a sense of wonder. Rooted in Christian values but welcoming all faiths, the school fosters reflection and unity through assemblies that include moments of quiet stillness.
Growth
Without exception, every child has huge potential and at St. Helen’s College we help our children to fulfil this through guidance, encouragement and challenge. As children become aware of their growing aptitudes and talents they develop the self-motivation and strength of character required for success.
Well-Being And Personal Development
The St. Helen’s College approach to education is genuinely holistic; as well as academic, creative and physical development, we place great value on personal development.
All areas of school life and all members of staff are influential in fostering the personal development of the pupils. The main classroom focus is in our weekly PSHE lessons, led by the form teachers. Our innovative programme supports every child to thrive.
Philosophy (P4C)
Children from Nursery to Year 6 experience Philosophy for Children (P4C). The children are given a stimulus and they devise a ‘deep’ question which is then discussed. Through hearing each other’s ideas, children get to know each other better and learn how to respect the opinions of others.
Mindfulness
The school follows the excellent courses developed by the Mindfulness in Schools Project (MiSP) to support emotional resilience. Mindfulness practices are embedded throughout the school and ensure the children are well equipped with tools to manage any challenges that they may face.
Peer Support
St. Helen’s College children learn the skills needed to counsel each other and resolve disputes before needing teacher intervention. Throughout the school, trained children play the part of ‘Playground Pals’, caring for each other in the playground and mediating disagreements.
Positive Psychology
The children follow a course in Year 5 which teaches them to watch their thoughts and choose not to think negatively. They learn to do kind acts and how to be still and that happiness often comes through helping others.
Onsite Counsellor
The school has a fully qualified children’s counsellor onsite to support pupils who require extra support to manage particular worries or anxieties during difficult times.

Welcome to St. Helen’s College
We believe that we have something unique and special to offer the children who attend our school.
For 100 years, St. Helen’s College has been renowned for its family atmosphere and its warm, welcoming environment. We pride ourselves on the exceptional care and attention we give to each individual pupil, encouraging them to be the best they can possibly be. Our pupils strive for and achieve excellence, not only academically but in their all-round endeavours too.
St. Helen’s College children are known locally for their courtesy and manners, their impeccable behaviour, and for their impressive achievements, not least in gaining places at top independent and grammar schools.
At St. Helen’s College we believe that giving children the very best education is built upon three principles: establishing lasting values, creating a harmonious environment and inspiring the pursuit of excellence.
When our pupils leave us at the end of Year 6 they do so as well rounded and confident young people with strong values, and skills. They are full of aspirations and ideas and ready for the wider world of senior schools, university and beyond.

Nursery
Explore Nursery
Providing the highest standard of care, support and education.
St. Helen’s College Nursery, open year-round from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., provides outstanding education and care for children aged 2 to 4 years.
Where curiosity begins and confidence grows
Our Nursery is an integrated part of our Lower School, making full use of the grounds and facilities. A dedicated, secure outdoor area with age-appropriate equipment for young children is also accessed daily.
All of our staff members are fully qualified, dedicated and experienced Early Years specialists. Our staff expertise, underpinned by a deep understanding of child development, enables us to deliver outstanding support for each individual child during this crucial early stage of learning.
A nurturing environment where children thrive
We prioritise a generous staff-to-pupil ratio, which allows us to develop a deep knowledge of each child and to spend meaningful time with them, helping every child reach their full potential. Our teaching draws on a blend of approaches, including the Early Learning Goals, the Characteristics of Effective Teaching and Learning, elements of the Montessori approach and interactive reading.
By integrating these methods with an emphasis on hands-on learning and developing real-world skills, we create a unique and creative curriculum that encourages children to take risks confidently and to feel comfortable tackling challenges as part of their learning journey.
Learning and development throughout our early years
Ducklings – 2 to 3 Years
Our Ducklings pupils learn through play, exploration, and imagination. Our pupils successfully build early social skills, develop language through songs and stories, strengthen coordination with climbing, painting and puzzles, enjoy sensory fun like sand and water play, and practise simple self-help routines.
Our vibrant curriculum supports every child to make friends, learn to share and work together. Our Ducklings grow in confidence through storytelling and role play, build early literacy and mathematical skills such as counting and recognising shapes and colours, and refine fine motor skills with cutting, gluing and drawing – all while expressing creativity through art, music and pretend play.
Each day includes free play, stories, outdoor adventures, creative activities and small-group learning, providing the perfect blend of learning, care and fun.
Cygnets – 3 to 4 Years
Our Cygnet pupils enjoy a rich, play-based environment that nurtures independence, confidence and curiosity. They develop strong social skills by forming friendships, collaborating in group activities, and beginning to solve conflicts with support.
Language flourishes through storytelling, show-and-tell, imaginative role play and early phonics games. Early literacy and mathematical skills grow as children recognise letters and sounds, write simple marks or letters, count with accuracy, compare quantities and explore shapes and patterns.
Physical development is strengthened through climbing, balancing, sports-style games and fine-motor activities like cutting, threading and early writing practice.
Creativity thrives through art, music, dance and small-world play, while curiosity is encouraged through simple science experiments, nature exploration and problem-solving challenges.
Each day blends free play, focused small-group learning, outdoor discovery, creative projects and calm moments – supporting children as they become confident, school-ready learners.

A time of growth and preparation
Upper School is where children take exciting steps forward in their learning. Our curriculum is carefully designed to ensure academic progress while fostering creativity, resilience, and independence.
Preparation for Senior School assessments at 11+ is seamlessly woven into everyday learning, giving pupils the skills and self-belief they need to shine.
All-round development
Life in Upper School is rich and varied. Alongside academic progress, pupils develop socially and physically through sports fixtures, residential trips, and opportunities to take on responsibility. They learn personal organisation skills, enjoy more specialist teaching, and take part in weekly 11+ practice sessions.
Leadership and community are central to this stage. Pupils elect peers to the School Council, Eco-Council, and Charity Council, and as the oldest members of the school, they become inspiring role models for younger children.
Working together for your child’s future
Choosing the right Senior School is an important milestone, and we are here to guide you every step of the way. We offer:
Information Meetings
Join the Head and Senior Leadership Team for friendly, informative sessions about Senior School options and transfer processes.
Bespoke Advice
Every family meets one-to-one with the Head to discuss your child’s unique strengths and aspirations. Together, we begin to shape a clear, personalised pathway for their next stage.
A Partnership Built on Care
We work closely with every family to ensure each child is supported, understood and ready for their next chapter.
Our goals and aims
At St. Helen’s College, we believe in working hand-in-hand with families to ensure every child feels supported and prepared for the exciting opportunities ahead.
Our goal is simple: to help your child thrive, both now and in the future.
Celebrating our outstanding 11+ success
We are extremely proud of our outstanding 11+ results in academic subjects, sport, music and drama. Our pupils transfer at 11+ to some of the best independent and maintained schools in the country.

Foundations For Learning
The Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum
The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) sets the national standards for all Early Years educators, ensuring that children learn and develop well in a healthy and safe environment. It supports high-quality teaching and learning so that every child builds a broad base of knowledge and skills – providing the right foundation for future success in school and beyond.
As a legal framework for all Early Years providers working with children from birth to five, the EYFS guides how we create our learning environment, shape our curriculum and support every child in our Nursery. We use the tenets of the EYFS curriculum as a foundation to ensure that each child is nurtured, challenged and encouraged to achieve their very best.
The EYFS also outlines the key outcomes children should reach by the end of their Reception year. It ensures we consider every aspect of children’s development and organises learning into seven interconnected areas, helping us provide a balanced and holistic early education for every child.
Outdoor Learning
Exploring nature through play and discovery
We believe that outdoor play is a vital part of every child’s learning journey and we embrace it in all weathers, from the moment children join our Nursery. Whether through nature sessions in our wooded area, welly walking on a rainy day or exploring our green outdoor spaces and school Zen Garden, children have regular opportunities to connect with nature. They learn to care for the world around them, notice the changing seasons, and experience the joy of fresh air and open space. From Nursery, our pupils are encouraged to partake in our Eco Team initiatives and to have an active voice in how we care for our environment.
By encouraging children to explore and enjoy the natural world, we help them not only to show empathy, but also to develop resilience, curiosity and a lasting respect for our planet.
Specialist Teaching
Building successful breadth of learning
From the age of 2, our Nursery pupils can begin their learning in Spanish, with music, P.E. and drama also commencing once the children move to the Cygnets class aged 3 to 4. These specialist-led lessons with teaching staff fully qualified in their respective subject, are integrated weekly into the Nursery timetable and offer every child the opportunity to explore and develop new interests, skills and experience breadth of learning.

Inspiring learning from the very start
At St. Helen’s College Pre-Prep, we offer a rich and engaging curriculum designed to nurture the whole child and spark a lifelong love of learning. From Reception, children continue to develop their Spanish language skills through fun and interactive songs, stories and games. They also benefit from specialist-led lessons in music, drama and P.E., providing every child the chance to explore and develop their unique talents and interests.

We believe that rich, hands-on experiences play a crucial role in deepening pupils’ understanding and enjoyment of the curriculum. Each year group – from Nursery through to Year 1 – participates in a range of exciting workshops and educational visits, carefully chosen to complement and enhance classroom learning.
By offering diverse, high-quality learning opportunities, we help every child thrive academically, socially and emotionally, laying a strong foundation for their educational journey. Prep
The Curriculum
At St. Helen’s College we offer a curriculum that is broad, balanced and exciting, designed to challenge and inspire every pupil.
Our approach goes beyond academic achievement; we aim to nurture a lifelong love of learning and a sense of wonder in every classroom.
Developing the whole learner
Curiosity lies at the heart of our teaching. Pupils are encouraged to question, explore and think critically, developing independence and creativity alongside strong academic foundations. Through high-quality, ambitious teaching, we tailor learning to reflect the individual needs of each child while fostering confidence and resilience.
Across all subjects, learning is underpinned by a focus on essential skills such as co-operation, resilience, and curiosity. These qualities are not taught in isolation – they are woven into every lesson, ensuring pupils not only acquire knowledge but also develop the personal attributes needed to thrive in an ever-changing world.
A balanced and enriching curriculum
At St. Helen’s College Prep, we provide a well-structured and balanced curriculum that ensures every child receives the time and attention needed to thrive. In Years 3 to 6, English and Mathematics remain the foundation of learning, with five hours per week dedicated to each subject.
Pupils also enjoy a broad range of subjects: Science (2 – 2.5 hours weekly), Art (1.5 hours), Computing (1 hour), Drama (30 minutes), Music (1 hour), and Physical Education (2.5 hours). Personal development is supported through PSHE (1 hour) and Religious Education (1 hour), alongside opportunities to explore Geography, History, and Spanish, each allocated between 1–2 hours weekly.
Additionally, Reasoning is taught for 1 hour per week in Years 3 and 4, helping pupils develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills. This structured approach ensures depth and variety, equipping pupils with essential skills and knowledge while fostering creativity and curiosity.
Personalised support and academic progress
Pupil progress is closely monitored by both staff and pupils themselves, with regular reflection and assessment informing individual targets and shaping the direction of teaching and curriculum planning. This ensures that learning remains responsive, purposeful and personalised.
At St. Helen’s College we believe education should be an adventure: broad, challenging and full of opportunities to grow. By combining academic excellence with character development, we prepare our pupils to become confident, capable and compassionate learners.
Academic Enrichment
Bringing learning to life beyond the classroom
At St. Helen’s College, school trips, visits and residentials significantly enrich our curriculum by providing meaningful, engaging and memorable experiences that bring learning to life. These opportunities deepen pupils’ subject knowledge by strengthening their understanding, allowing them to apply what they have learned in real‑world contexts and helping them make purposeful connections beyond the classroom.
All children enjoy termly day trips to castles, museums, gardens, educational centres and theatres. In Prep (Year 3 onwards) they attend residential trips to Sayers Croft Outdoor Learning Centre, Flatford Mill field study centre in Suffolk, to Little Canada on the Isle of Wight to study coastal erosion and for adventurous outdoor activities, and to Andalucia in southern Spain for a week of immersion in Spanish language and culture.
Our residential trips promote personal growth, building independence, resilience, teamwork and confidence, while also supporting academic progress through the development of key skills such as problem‑solving and communication. We also regularly welcome visiting speakers who share specialist expertise, career insights and diverse perspectives, broadening pupils’ horizons and inspiring curiosity, ambition and a lifelong love of learning.

The Leadership Team
Senior Management Staff
Meet the passionate leaders of St. Helen’s College.
St. Helen’s College is a school built on family values and has a passionate, caring and highly experienced team of staff who are committed to maintaining excellent standards across the school, and to champion the success of each individual child.
Our Senior Leadership Team are skilled professional leaders at the forefront of education who are excellently positioned to inspire staff and lead the school with the pupils at its heart.

Ms. Jo Matthews

Ms. Sophie Green
Sophie began her Headship at Herries Preparatory School in Cookham Dean, a co-educational setting for pupils aged 3–11, before joining Godstowe, a leading Prep school for girls. During her tenure at Godstowe, she successfully guided pupils through the Buckinghamshire 11+ grammar school process and in recognition of her leadership, she was named Tatler magazine ‘Prep Head of the Year’ in her final year. After leaving Godstowe in 2022, Sophie joined St. Helen’s College as Head in 2025. She is a trained and experienced ISI Inspector. Beyond school life, Sophie enjoys reading detective novels, cooking, walking, going to the gym, visiting art galleries, and travelling.
Ms. Jo Matthews
A graduate in Psychology, Jo began her career as an Assistant Psychologist, supporting young children with a range of special educational needs. It was here that she discovered her passion for teaching in early years. After gaining her teaching degree, Jo went on to lead a team across several schools in Staffordshire, in a pilot Government initiative to bring improved reading and phonics provision into primary schools, before joining St. Helen’s College in 2005 as a Reception teacher. During her time at the school, she has taken the lead in computing, CPD and early years. In 2013, Jo gained Chartered Teacher Status with the Chartered College of Teaching and now supports them as a Research Champion. More recently, she undertook further studies, completing a master’s degree in early years education. Beyond school, Jo enjoys illustration, literature, attending the theatre, and spending time on family holidays with her partner and two teenage children.
Mr. Steve Roche
Deputy Head Academic
Steve has worked across a number of independent school settings, developing a deep passion for the sector and its holistic approach to education. He began his leadership journey as Head of English, before progressing to his current role, where he oversees curriculum innovation, teaching and learning strategies, and academic standards. A published children’s book author, Steve brings creativity and a love of literature into his work, inspiring pupils to think critically and imaginatively. He values the warm, nurturing atmosphere at St. Helen’s College and is committed to fostering pupil wellbeing, drawing on his interest in mindfulness and psychology to support both staff and students. Beyond school life, Steve enjoys hiking, reading, and exploring tea culture.
Mrs. Melanie Gilbert
Deputy Head Pastoral
Melanie began her career at St Hilda’s School in Bushey, an independent prep school for girls aged 3-11. During her time at the school, she held the roles of Head of House and Assessment Coordinator as a member of the Senior Leadership Team, which provided her with a strong foundation in pastoral care and teaching and learning. Melanie also led the school in becoming one of the pioneer schools for Empathy Lab, an organisation that uses literature to build children’s empathy, helping them to understand others and contribute to a kinder society. She was appointed as Deputy Head of St Hilda’s School in September 2022 and joined St. Helen’s College in 2025. Melanie is passionate about creating opportunities for every child to flourish, placing their wellbeing and pastoral care at the heart of everything she does. Outside of work, she enjoys running, going to the theatre, dog walking, reading and travelling.
Mrs. Elaine Coyle
Elaine began her career in childcare 23 years ago and has been working at St. Helen’s College for 14 years. She has worked across the Lower School including the 2+ and 3+ Nursery settings, as well as in Reception, and managed the school Holiday Club for three years. Elaine is passionate about working with young children to provide a high-quality Early Years education and positive start to their school life. Elaine was appointed Nursery Manager at the new year-round St. Helen’s College provision in 2025. She is a trained Mini Me Yoga practitioner and outside of school she enjoys looking after her horses, dogs and chickens, meeting up with friends and reading.

ISI Report September 2024
St. Helen’s College received an “Excellent” report
St. Helen’s College was inspected by the ISI (Independent Schools Inspectorate) in September 2024 and received an excellent report, recognising the enormous passion, expertise and commitment of our staff to ensure superb outcomes for our pupils.
In particular, we are delighted that inspectors recognised the exceptional oral communication skills of our pupils by awarding St. Helen’s College a rare ‘area of significant strength’. Inspectors said,
“Leaders have high aspirations for pupils. The decision to prioritise oracy skills and to provide opportunities for pupils to use them, results in highly articulate, confident individuals. Pupils readily express their thoughts and opinions. This is a significant strength of the school. Pupils use verbal reasoning skills to explain their independent thinking. They are empowered to be dynamic individuals who lead initiatives that make a positive and impactful contribution to the school and wider community.”

Leadership and Culture
Experienced leaders foster a culture of excellence through harmony, aligning with the school’s motto. Staff are encouraged to prioritise pupil wellbeing, recognising each child’s unique potential to thrive.

Strong communication and continued involvement from former proprietors have ensured stability during the transition to new ownership. Leaders and governors collaborate effectively, making sound decisions and meeting all regulatory standards.
Oracy and Pupil Empowerment
Leaders set high expectations, with a focus on developing oracy skills that result in articulate, confident pupils. Students express themselves clearly and lead initiatives that positively impact the school and wider community.
Early Years Foundation
The early years curriculum balances nurturing care with academic challenge, starting with strong oracy development in Nursery. Positive relationships and specialist teaching create a supportive learning environment.
Curriculum and Assessment
The curriculum is thoughtfully designed to build knowledge and skills, with systematic checks ensuring leaders understand pupil progress. Tools like learning logs personalise learning.
Wellbeing and Emotional Development
Mental health is a priority, creating a calm and reflective atmosphere where pupils feel happy and supported. Activities like yoga and mindfulness foster emotional regulation and resilience, encouraging confident risk-taking.

Leaders know pupils well and respond quickly to concerns, supported by open communication and mutual respect. This contributes to excellent behaviour and a strong sense of pride in the school community.

Leaders maintain a strong safeguarding culture, working closely with external agencies to address risks. Their timely responses and meticulous records ensure pupil safety across all areas.

School Life
Co-curricular & Wraparound Care
Co-curricular activities allow children to explore their interests and develop their talents at the same time as having fun!
The St. Helen’s College philosophy is that, from a young age, our pupils should have the opportunity to try as many different activities as possible, to give them the widest possible chance of discovering a lifelong passion or talent.
Opportunities for every child
Our co-curricular programme is therefore unique and very diverse. All pupils are encouraged to take a full part in the programme, and participation levels are high. A wide variety of traditional and non-traditional creative, academic, dramatic, musical and sporting clubs are offered throughout the year to all year groups from Reception to Year 6.
Each term’s programme is published to parents, who make bookings for clubs through their SchoolsBuddy account.
Most clubs are available to all children in the relevant year group(s); some clubs are ‘by invitation’ to selected children only following auditions, team trials etc.
Sample Co-curricular Timetable Sample Co-curricular Timetable Sample Co-curricular Timetable
There are so many activities. There really is something for everyone.
A Parent
Wraparound Care
The St. Helen’s College Wraparound Care services are available to children from Reception to Year 6 and provide a seamless and flexible service to support busy working parents. Our clubs are led by our own staff, many of whom have worked at St. Helen’s College for many years and are very familiar to the children and their families.
Funtasia Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club runs from 7.30 a.m. to 8.00 a.m. every school day. Children are provided with a healthy breakfast and may take part in quiet activities. They are supervised by the staff, who then accompany the children to join their classes.
Funtasia After School Club
Our After School Club runs from 3.00 p.m. to 6.00 p.m. every school day, at both the Upper and the Lower School. The children are given time to play, after which they have a light tea together. Homework follows for the older children, then the children take part in a wide range of activities, which might include football or tennis in the playground, computing, cooking, art and craft, playing with toys, scrambling on the adventure playground, or quietly drawing, reading or colouring.
Funtasia Holiday Club
The Holiday Club runs throughout the school holidays, with a break only at Christmas. It is run by the After School Club staff and even some of our teaching staff who choose to work during the holidays, so there are many familiar faces for the children. They enjoy a programme of fun activities, with a different theme each week or holiday period. Recent themes have included Easter, Tropical Islands and Well Being.

About Us
Our Approach to Learning
Inspiring Minds, Shaping Futures
At St. Helen’s College, we take a holistic approach to education, balancing essential knowledge with the development of learning skills that prepare children for life.
Every lesson is designed to challenge, engage and inspire, with quality teaching at its core. Beyond acquiring knowledge, pupils develop the ability to learn effectively. They engage in self-reflection, identify their strengths, set meaningful goals, and gain a deep understanding of the learning process. St. Helen’s College children are empowered to become confident, independent thinkers who approach challenges with curiosity and creativity.
Specialist Teaching and Continuous Excellence
From the earliest years, children are taught by specialist educators with deep subject knowledge and a genuine passion for their field. This expertise ensures that every lesson is rich, engaging, and delivered to the highest standard.
Our teachers are passionate educators and lifelong learners. They regularly undertake continuous professional development (CPD), staying at the forefront of educational research and best practice. This commitment guarantees that excellent teaching is delivered across all subjects, every day.

Technology That Brings Learning to Life
Technology is carefully integrated into our curriculum to create lessons which are dynamic, interactive, and inspiring. From tools that spark creativity to platforms that encourage collaboration and independent exploration, technology enhances learning and helps ensure every child feels engaged and is prepared for the digital world.
Exceptional Support
With an exceptional staff-to-pupil ratio, we build close, supportive relationships that help every child thrive. Collaborative teaching is a key feature of our approach, offering pupils the benefit of varied perspectives and personalised guidance. Alongside our teachers, a dedicated team of Teaching and Learning Assistants works in partnership to ensure every child feels valued, challenged, and celebrated.
